Aarhus is Denmark's largest seaport and city on Jutland Peninsula's eastern coast. It is located approx 187 km (116 mi) northwest of Copenhagen (country's capital) and approx 290 km (180 mi) north of Hamburg Germany. The city has population around 275,000 (metro around 340,000), ranking it Denmark's second-largest (after Copenhagen).

Among the well-known tourist attractions are ARoS Art Museum, Old Town Museum, Tivoli Friheden (amusement park), Moesgård Museum, Kvindemuseet (Women's Museum), The city is also a great shopping destination. Most foreign tourists are from Norway, Sweden, Germany and the UK. Overall annual tourist spending in the city is around USD 540 million. The average hotel stay is 3 days.

Port Aarhus

Port Aarhus (locode DKAAR) is Denmark's largest and also one of northern Europe's biggest cargo ports (ranked 1st among the 200+ Baltic Sea cargo ports). It has the country's largest containership terminal handling over 1/2 of the country's container shipping traffic, 60% of the bulk cargo traffic and capacity to berth world's largest boxships.

The port is located at the mouth of Aarhus River in Kattegat Sea, facing Helgenæs peninsula (east), Samso Island (southeast) and Riis Skov forest park (north). The seaport is self-governing and financially independent company managed by the municipality. Here are handled around 9,5 million cargo tons per year. The principal export is grain. Main imports include stone, cement, coal.

The port has all 6 terminals - containership, multi-use, for bulk carriers, for oil tankers, ferries and cruise liners.

  • Container Terminal has pier length 1,300 km, water depth (max draft) 14 m and is served by 8 gantry cranes (3 Post-Panamax, 4 Super Post-Panamax and 1 Panamax).
  • Multi-use Terminal serves bulk carriers (shipping mainly coal and feedstuffs), also project cargo (wood, windmills).
  • Bulk Terminal serves loose cargo carriers shipping mainly grain, sand, gravel, cement.
  • Tanker Terminal serves ships carrying mineral oils, gasoline, molasses, also chemical tankers.

Aarhus Ferry Terminal is used mainly by MOLSLINJEN ferries, serving annually ~1 million vehicles and ~2 million passengers. Aarhus Cruise Terminal serves cruise ships with Baltic Sea itineraries, operated between March and November.

The Container Terminal is operated under concession by APM Terminals Aarhus - part of APM Terminals (2001-founded, The Hague Holland-based port and terminals management company, one of the world's largest). In 2020, APM Aarhus handled 593,670 TEU-containers (13% increase over 2019). APM Aarhus handles ~60% of Denmark's boxship traffic.

In 2016 was inaugurated a regular flight service (via floatplanes) from Aarhus to Copenhagen, with fly time ~40 min (train travel time is ~3 hours).

Aarhus Ferry Terminal is currently the only alternative to Storebæltsforbindelsen (Great Belt Fixed Link) that crosses the strait between the islands Zealand and Funen. The route is served with regularly scheduled ferries since 1830. The current main ferry operator is MOLSLINJEN, with annual traffic ~2 million passengers and 1 million vehicles. Ro-Ro ships (cargo ferries) link Aarhus to Kalundborg and Finland (regular weekly service).

Aarhus is also becoming a cruise port destination for companies operating on Baltic Sea itineraries. In 2010, it was visited by just 2 ships and ~4300 tourists. In 2012 it handled 18 ship calls and over 38,000 passengers. In 2013 were handled 13 cruise calls. In 2018 were booked 41 cruise ship berthings with estimated nearly 100,000 passengers.

In March 2022, Port Aarhus contracted Shore Link OU (Tallinn Estonia-based engineering company specializing in port shorepower solutions) and PowerCon AS (Hadsund Denmark-based manufacturing company specializing in wind turbines) to design, supply and install a shore-power system. Shoreside power capabilities allow berthed vessels to turn off their diesel engines and instead use the city's power-grid electricity for onboard operations and services. The new system (inaugurated in June 2023) has a separate "CMS Cruiser"/smaller capacity unit designed exclusively for cruise liners. The other Danish cruise port with shore power capabilities is Copenhagen.

Aarhus Port's shore-power facility was inaugurated on June 20, 2023, with AIDAmar ship. The system's total cost was EUR 7 million, of which 5M from the Port, 1M from the city and 1M from the European Union. The energy provider is the local company KONSTANT Net AS.

Aarhus cruise terminal

Port Aarhus welcomes cruise ship passengers with live performances by Den Jyske Pigegarde (orchestra and dance girls aged 8-25) - usually a folk dance show. The terminal is located across the street from downtown. The quay was extensively improved in 2012.

Since 2018, cruise passengers in Aarhus are welcomed by local hosts. These are around 1300 volunteers serving as hosts for cruisers. They all wear blue t-shirts and badgets signed "ASK ME", and assist the disembarking tourists with various cultural events in the city.

Aarhus cruise port is located 3 hours from Copenhagen by bus. There are bus connections to Hamburg too. The closest airport is Tirstrup (45 min by bus).

At a Glance

Independent sightseeing: Easy independently from the main cruise quay. Aarhus is one of the more convenient Scandinavian cruise calls for exploring on foot. Ships normally dock rather than tender, and the main cruise quay at Balticagade is close to the historic centre. Port of Aarhus also uses the more distant Omni Terminal for some calls, so check your ship's berth before planning a walking day.

  • Main cruise quay: roughly 1 km (0.6 mi) from the central shopping and cathedral area, around 10–15 minutes on foot.
  • Terrain: mostly flat, paved city streets; cobbles occur in parts of the historic centre.
  • Best independent choices: historic centre, Latin Quarter, ARoS Art Museum and Den Gamle By.
  • Transport useful for: Moesgaard Museum, the southern coastline and attractions outside central Aarhus.

Getting from the Cruise Port

The usual cruise quay is at Balticagade in the harbour immediately southeast of central Aarhus. From here, DOKK1 on the waterfront is approximately 0.7 km (0.4 mi) away, while Aarhus Cathedral and the central pedestrian streets are about 1 km (0.6 mi) from the cruise area.

Walking is normally the simplest option. The route into town is largely level, and once in the centre most major sights are close enough to combine without transport.

Some cruise ships can instead berth at the Port of Aarhus Omni Terminal, which is farther inside the commercial harbour. If your ship is assigned there, do not use walking times from the Balticagade cruise quay; follow the transfer and passenger-exit arrangements announced for your particular call.

Aarhus has city buses and the Letbanen light rail. DOKK1 is a useful transport point near the waterfront. Tickets for Aarhus city buses and light rail should be purchased before boarding, so passengers planning to use public transport should arrange a ticket through the available ticketing apps or other official sales channels before travelling.

Best Ways to Spend Your Time

Historic Centre, Cathedral and Latin Quarter

Allow: about 2–3 hours. Independent: very easy.

For a short call, walking into central Aarhus gives the best return for your time. Continue from DOKK1 toward Store Torv and Aarhus Cathedral, then explore the small streets of the Latin Quarter, Lille Torv, the Aarhus River and the pedestrian shopping area. Salling Rooftop can be added for an elevated city view when accessible.

This option needs no transport and can easily be shortened if the ship has an early departure.

ARoS Aarhus Art Museum

Allow: about 2–3 hours including the walk. Independent: easy.

ARoS is approximately 2 km (1.2 mi) from the main cruise quay and is practical on foot in roughly 25 minutes. Its best-known feature is the rooftop Your rainbow panorama, but allow enough time for the galleries if art is your main priority.

ARoS combines particularly well with the cathedral, Møllestien and the riverfront on the walk back toward the ship.

Den Gamle By – The Old Town Museum

Allow: about 3–4 hours. Independent: easy with a longer walk or local transport.

Den Gamle By is an extensive open-air museum recreating Danish town life in different periods. It is roughly 2.5 km (1.6 mi) from the main cruise area, around a 30–35 minute walk depending on the route and pace.

Because the museum itself deserves at least a couple of hours, passengers with limited time may prefer to walk there through the centre and use a taxi or public transport for one direction. Much of the attraction is outdoors, so ARoS may be the more practical museum choice in poor weather.

Moesgaard Museum

Allow: about 3–4 hours including transport. Independent: practical with planning and public transport.

Moesgaard is outside central Aarhus and should be treated as a separate excursion rather than added casually to a city walk. It lies approximately 9 km (5.6 mi) south of central Aarhus and focuses on archaeology, prehistory and anthropology.

City bus 18 runs from the central Park Allé/Banegårdspladsen area directly to Moesgaard, with the bus journey taking about 25 minutes. A taxi is simpler when time ashore is tight. Combining Moesgaard, Den Gamle By and a thorough visit to ARoS in one normal cruise call would usually make the day unnecessarily rushed.

Southern Coast and the Infinite Bridge

Allow: about 2–3 hours with transport. Independent: possible, but transport is advisable.

The coastline south of central Aarhus combines beaches and Marselisborg woodland. The Infinite Bridge at Varna/Ballehage is a circular wooden walkway extending over Aarhus Bay and makes a good alternative for passengers more interested in scenery than museums.

The bridge is seasonal and is normally installed from spring until late October. It is better reached by local transport, taxi or bicycle than by walking all the way from the cruise ship during a limited port call.

Self-Guided Walking Tour

Harbour, Old Aarhus and ARoS Loop

Distance: approximately 5.5 km (3.4 mi). Pure walking time: about 70–80 minutes. Recommended total time: 3–4 hours with sightseeing stops. Difficulty: easy to moderate. Mostly level streets, with some cobbles and gentle gradients around ARoS and the western centre.

  1. Balticagade cruise quay: leave the main cruise area and walk toward central Aarhus along the harbour.
  2. DOKK1: pass the distinctive waterfront library and continue toward the historic centre.
  3. Store Torv and Aarhus Cathedral: explore the cathedral square and surrounding old streets.
  4. ARoS Aarhus Art Museum: continue southwest through the centre. Visit the museum if time allows, or simply use it as the turning point of the walk.
  5. Mølleparken and Møllestien: descend toward the Aarhus River and detour through the small cobbled street of Møllestien.
  6. Latin Quarter: continue via Vestergade and Lille Torv into the narrow streets north of the cathedral.
  7. Salling Rooftop and central pedestrian streets: add the rooftop viewpoint if time permits, then head back toward DOKK1.
  8. Return to Balticagade: follow the waterfront back to the cruise quay.

This route closely follows a locally recommended central Aarhus walk and works particularly well for cruise passengers because it begins and ends at the harbour. Skip the ARoS interior if you have less than three hours available ashore.

Practical Tips

  • Check your berth before leaving the ship. Walking guidance for the Balticagade cruise quay should not automatically be applied to calls using the Omni Terminal.
  • Central Aarhus is compact enough that public transport is unnecessary for a typical cathedral–Latin Quarter–ARoS sightseeing day.
  • Buy public-transport tickets before boarding city buses or the light rail.
  • For Moesgaard Museum or the southern coastline, allow extra time for the return journey rather than planning connections too close to all-aboard.
  • For sightseeing within central Aarhus, aim to be back in the port area comfortably before the ship's all-aboard time. Allow a larger margin when returning from attractions outside the centre or when your ship uses the Omni Terminal.
